_note: Super investors tracked by QWERTx. 'cik' is the SEC filer ID; 'expect' must appear in the SEC entity name or the investor is skipped (protects against a wrong CIK). Profile text (tags, meta, about, philosophy) appears on each investor page. The data workflow runs automatically when this file changes.

investors.about: Warren Buffett turned a struggling textile mill into Berkshire Hathaway, one of the largest companies in the world. He handed the CEO role to Greg Abel at the start of 2026 and remains chairman. Berkshire’s stock portfolio sits alongside its wholly owned businesses such as GEICO, BNSF Railway and Berkshire Hathaway Energy.
philosophy: Buy wonderful businesses at fair prices and hold them for a very long time.
Stay inside your circle of competence and demand a margin of safety.
Keep plenty of cash so you can act when others are fearful.

investors.meta: Pershing Square Capital Management · New York · since 2004
investors.about: Bill Ackman founded Pershing Square in 2004. He runs a small number of large, high-conviction positions in simple, predictable, cash-generating businesses, and sometimes pushes management for change. Part of the capital is permanent, through the London-listed Pershing Square Holdings.
philosophy: Own a handful of dominant, predictable businesses with high barriers to entry.
Engage with management when change can unlock value.
Use permanent capital so short-term swings don’t force selling.

investors.about: Sir Chris Hohn founded The Children’s Investment Fund (TCI) in 2003. It has been one of the best-performing large hedge funds, owning a few monopoly-like businesses with pricing power and pushing for change when needed.
philosophy: Own businesses with durable barriers to entry and pricing power.
Concentrate in your best ideas.
Engage hard when governance or strategy falls short.

investors.meta: Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation Trust · Seattle / Kirkland, Washington · since 2000
investors.about: The Gates Foundation Trust holds the foundation’s endowment, separate from its charitable work. Its large Berkshire Hathaway stake comes from Warren Buffett’s annual gifts, which the trust sells over time to fund the foundation’s grants.
philosophy: Preserve capital to fund decades of grant-making.
Hold durable, high-quality companies.
Steady, long-term stewardship rather than trading.

investors.meta: H&H International Investment · Palo Alto, California · since 2000s
investors.about: Duan Yongping founded the electronics group behind brands like BBK, OPPO and vivo, and was an early backer of PDD. A devoted student of Warren Buffett, he invests his family’s money through H&H International with very few, very large positions.
philosophy: Do the right things, and do them right.
Only buy what you understand and would own for ten years.
Very few decisions, held with patience.

investors.about: Bill Nygren manages flagship funds at Oakmark, the fund family of Chicago-based Harris Associates. The firm buys companies trading well below its estimate of intrinsic value; the 13F covers all of Harris Associates’ US holdings.
philosophy: Buy businesses trading at a big discount to intrinsic value.
Invest with managers who think like owners.
Sell when price approaches value, then repeat.

investors.meta: Tiger Global Management · New York · since 2001
investors.about: Chase Coleman, a “Tiger Cub” trained by Julian Robertson, founded Tiger Global in 2001. The public equity book focuses on global internet, software and AI leaders.
philosophy: Back the long-term winners of technology shifts.
Combine deep fundamental research with a global lens.
Size positions by conviction and earnings growth.

investors.meta: Lone Pine Capital · Greenwich, Connecticut · since 1997
investors.about: Stephen Mandel, another Tiger Cub, founded Lone Pine in 1997 and later stepped back from day-to-day management, which passed to a new generation of portfolio managers. The firm is known for high-turnover, research-driven growth investing.
philosophy: Find businesses whose growth the market underestimates.
Do intense, bottom-up research on management and competition.
Rotate quickly when the thesis changes.

investors.about: Terry Smith founded Fundsmith in 2010 with a strategy that fits on a single page. The firm owns high-quality global companies that need little debt and earn high returns on capital. The 13F covers its US-listed holdings.
philosophy: Buy good companies.
Don’t overpay.
Do nothing.

investors.about: Tom Gayner is CEO of Markel Group, a specialty insurer and holding company that is often compared to Berkshire. He has run the equity portfolio for decades using four simple filters.
philosophy: Profitable businesses with good returns and little debt.
Management teams with equal talent and integrity.
Reinvestment opportunities, at a fair price.

investors.meta: Icahn Capital Management · Sunny Isles Beach, Florida · since 1968
investors.about: Carl Icahn is one of the best-known activist investors in history, taking large stakes and pushing for board seats, buybacks or sales. Most of his capital is tied to Icahn Enterprises (IEP), which is also his largest reported holding.
philosophy: Buy when a company is out of favour and management can be challenged.
Shareholders, not managers, should decide a company’s direction.
Be willing to stand alone against consensus.

investors.meta: Appaloosa Management · Miami Beach, Florida · since 1993
investors.about: David Tepper built Appaloosa into one of the most successful hedge funds of its era, famous for bold, well-timed bets after market panics. The firm now mainly manages Tepper’s own money and moves quickly between sectors and themes.
philosophy: Be aggressive when fear is at its highest and prices reflect it.
Follow policy and the economic cycle, not just company stories.
Change your mind fast when the facts change.

investors.meta: Oaktree Capital Management · Los Angeles · since 1995
investors.about: Howard Marks co-founded Oaktree, a global leader in credit and distressed investing; Brookfield owns a majority of the firm. His memos to clients are required reading on market cycles and risk. Oaktree’s 13F includes stocks, convertible bonds and index puts used for hedging.
philosophy: You can’t predict the future, but you can know where we are in the cycle.
Second-level thinking: ask what everyone else is missing.
Risk means the chance of permanent loss, not volatility.

investors.meta: Akre Capital Management · Middleburg, Virginia · since 1989
investors.about: Chuck Akre founded Akre Capital around his “three-legged stool”: extraordinary businesses, run by talented and honest managers, with great ways to reinvest their cash. Day-to-day management passed to his successors John Neff and Chris Cerrone.
philosophy: Own extraordinary businesses with high returns on capital.
Back managers with integrity and talent.
Look for great reinvestment opportunities, then sit still.

investors.about: Daniel Loeb founded Third Point in 1995. The firm mixes event-driven and activist investing across stocks and credit, and is known for pointed letters to company boards.
philosophy: Look for catalysts that can close the gap between price and value.
Engage directly when management falls short.
Move nimbly across asset classes.

investors.about: Li Lu founded Himalaya Capital in 1997 and is a long-time partner of the late Charlie Munger, who entrusted part of his family’s money to him. Himalaya runs a very concentrated portfolio of US and Asian businesses.
philosophy: Think like an owner of the whole business, not a trader of its stock.
Concentrate on the few ideas you understand deeply.
Let compounding work over decades.

investors.about: Prem Watsa built Fairfax, a Toronto-based insurance and investment holding company often called “Canada’s Berkshire”. He invests the insurance float with a long-term, contrarian value mindset, frequently in out-of-favour areas.
philosophy: Buy when others are selling, with a margin of safety.
Protect the downside first; returns will follow.
Fair and friendly long-term partnerships with management.

investors.about: Seth Klarman leads Baupost, a Boston firm known for patient, risk-averse value investing and a willingness to hold lots of cash. Much of Baupost’s capital sits in private deals, real estate and credit, so the 13F shows only its US-listed stock positions.
philosophy: A margin of safety comes first: avoid permanent loss of capital.
Look where others are forced or unwilling to sell.
Holding cash is fine when bargains are scarce.

investors.meta: Pabrai Investment Funds · Irvine, California · since 1999
investors.about: Mohnish Pabrai runs the Pabrai Investment Funds and the Dakshana Foundation. He follows a “heads I win, tails I don’t lose much” approach of few bets, rare bets and big bets. Many of his holdings trade outside the US, so the 13F (filed by Dalal Street, LLC) shows only the US-listed slice.
philosophy: Few bets, big bets, infrequent bets.
Clone the best ideas of great investors shamelessly.
Low risk, high uncertainty situations are where the bargains hide.

investors.meta: Trian Fund Management · New York · since 2005
investors.about: Nelson Peltz co-founded Trian with Peter May and Ed Garden. Trian buys large stakes in underperforming, well-known companies and works with, or presses, boards to improve operations and focus.
philosophy: Great brands can underperform because of strategy, not because of the business.
Operational change and focus unlock value.
Be patient and constructive, but persistent.

investors.meta: Duquesne Family Office · New York · since 1981
investors.about: Stanley Druckenmiller ran Duquesne Capital for three decades without a losing year and was lead portfolio manager for George Soros’s Quantum Fund. Since 2010 he has managed his own money through the Duquesne Family Office, shifting quickly between themes as the macro picture changes.
philosophy: Make big bets when conviction is high, and cut losses quickly when wrong.
Follow liquidity and central banks: they drive markets more than earnings.
Stay flexible; no position is permanent.

investors.meta: Greenlight Capital (files as DME Capital Management) · New York · since 1996
investors.about: David Einhorn founded Greenlight Capital in 1996 and became known for detailed short theses and contrarian value investing. Greenlight’s 13F holdings are now reported under DME Capital Management.
philosophy: Buy undervalued companies that the market misunderstands.
Do deep, independent research and be willing to stand alone.
Hedge with shorts; protect capital when markets look expensive.

investors.meta: ARK Investment Management · St. Petersburg, Florida · since 2014
investors.about: Cathie Wood founded ARK Invest in 2014 to invest in disruptive innovation: artificial intelligence, robotics, genomics, fintech and blockchain. Her flagship ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) became one of the best-known actively managed funds in the world, famous for big swings in both directions. This page shows ARK’s quarterly 13F; ARK also publishes its ETF holdings every trading day.
philosophy: Invest in innovation platforms that can change how the world works.
Think in five-year time frames, not quarters.
Concentrate in high-conviction ideas and lean in when they are out of favour.

investors.about: Tom Russo runs a concentrated portfolio of global consumer brands, often family-controlled companies like brewers, spirits makers and food businesses. He holds them for many years and looks for management willing to invest heavily today for growth years from now.
philosophy: Own brands that travel well into fast-growing markets.
Back managers with the “capacity to suffer”: reinvesting even when it hurts short-term profits.
Hold for decades and let compounding do the work.

investors.about: Guy Spier runs Aquamarine, a concentrated value fund modelled on Warren Buffett’s early partnerships. He is the author of The Education of a Value Investor and, with Mohnish Pabrai, bid for a charity lunch with Buffett in 2008.
philosophy: Own a few great businesses and trade very rarely.
Design your environment to avoid bad decisions: fewer screens, fewer meetings.
Use checklists to catch mistakes before they cost money.

investors.about: Bruce Berkowitz founded Fairholme and is known for extremely concentrated, contrarian bets, often holding a handful of companies for years. Real estate developer St. Joe has been his signature holding.
philosophy: Concentrate in the few ideas you know best.
Buy what others are afraid of, with a wide margin of safety.
Judge companies by the cash they generate, not reported earnings.

investors.meta: Gotham Asset Management · New York · since 1985
investors.about: Joel Greenblatt founded Gotham Capital in 1985, wrote The Little Book That Beats the Market (the “Magic Formula”) and has taught value investing at Columbia Business School. Gotham now runs systematic portfolios, so its 13F holds many stocks at small weights; look at the biggest positions and the changes.
philosophy: Buy good businesses (high return on capital) at bargain prices (high earnings yield).
Stick with a sound process through long stretches when it lags.
Value is about what a business is worth, not what the stock did lately.

investors.about: CPP Investments invests the Canada Pension Plan fund on behalf of Canadian workers and retirees, and is one of the largest pension investors in the world. Its 13F shows only its US-listed stocks, a small slice of a portfolio that also holds private equity, real estate, infrastructure, bonds and non-US shares.
philosophy: Invest for generations, not for the next quarter.
Diversify across assets, regions and strategies.
Use long horizons and scale as advantages.

investors.about: Fiera Capital is an independent Canadian asset manager listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (FSZ), running public and private market strategies for institutions and individuals. Its 13F combines the US-listed holdings of all its strategies.
philosophy: Combine public and private market strategies.
Focus on quality companies with durable growth.
Manage risk across many separate mandates.

investors.about: Founded by Stephen Jarislowsky in 1955, Jarislowsky Fraser is one of Canada’s best-known long-term investment firms and has been part of Scotiabank since 2018. It favours high-quality companies bought at sensible prices and held for years. The 13F shows its US-listed holdings only.
philosophy: Own quality companies with sustainable growth.
Pay a reasonable price and hold for the long term.
Avoid excessive debt and weak governance.

investors.about: Calgary-based Mawer is an independent, employee-owned Canadian manager known for its motto “be boring, make money”. It looks for wealth-creating businesses run by excellent managers, bought below their intrinsic value. The 13F shows its US-listed holdings only.
philosophy: Buy wealth-creating companies with excellent management at discounts to intrinsic value.
Be boring: patience and discipline over prediction.
Diversify thoughtfully and stay invested.

investors.about: Toronto-based Beutel Goodman is an employee-owned value manager. It buys companies trading at a discount to their business value, with a focus on free cash flow and balance-sheet strength. The 13F shows its US-listed holdings only.
philosophy: Buy at a discount to business value.
Focus on free cash flow and strong balance sheets.
Sell when prices reach business value; stay disciplined.
